Direct substitution supplies converse, kernel and section; span of r_c(a)=a+c gives d+1-dimensional inner group, and displacement products span d constants. originality.rationale: A publicly posted 2026 article explicitly asks for even-dihedral product automorphism groups and proves only a Latin (odd-modulus) case. The present full group structure addresses R4^d uniformly. A 2017 Corollary prints the larger inner rank 2^d and is explicitly contradicted by the computed d+1 rank. Broad affine-mesh theory and small tables are recognized as relevant antecedents; novelty remains qualified because unindexed literature may exist. Significant coverage risk is retained for Hou (2011), whose general theorem may subsume the full-group calculation but whose full statement was unavailable; the later explicit even-factor open question and the demonstrated correction of the 2017 inner-group formula support the qualified novelty of the evaluated result.
residual_risks: High relevance: X.-D. Hou, Automorphism groups of Alexander quandles (2011), covers general Alexander-quandle automorphisms by its abstract; its unavailable full text leaves exact implication comparison unresolved. This result may reduce the novelty of the explicit full-group specialization; the independent correction to Bardakov–Nasybullov–Singh (2017), Cor. 5.5, remains separately motivated.
The universal medial-quandle mesh isomorphism criterion might make this particular explicit formula obtainable as an unstated specialization.
An older unindexed result on 2-reductive/Takasaki quandles might explicitly compute the same group.
The published inner-group assertion is refuted only for the stated family; broader results of that paper are not reassessed here.
